title: MBTI vs Enneagram vs DISC vs Big Five for AI (Matcher)
description: Compare MBTI, Enneagram, DISC, Big Five (OCEAN), and Attachment for tuning AI assistants—plus an interactive 20-second matcher by workflow friction.
h1: Which personality system should you use to tune your AI?
dek: MBTI, Enneagram, DISC, Big Five (OCEAN), and Attachment control different layers of AI behavior—pick the exact template family in 20 seconds.
lede: AgentTune includes 43 MIT-licensed tuning templates across five personality systems, plus five free self-report quizzes. You do not need to take all five tests—or any test at all—to pick a great prompt. Each framework targets a different AI habit: cutting preamble (DISC / MBTI), adjusting one trait at a time (Big Five OCEAN), or calibrating pushback and warmth (Enneagram / Attachment).
answer: Use DISC or MBTI for faster bottom-line structure; use Big Five (OCEAN) to adjust a single trait (like High Openness or Low Extraversion) without adopting a full persona; and use Enneagram or Attachment to control how candidly the AI pushes back or cushions critique.

sections.h2: What our September 2026 benchmark data says about choosing between systems.
sections.html:
• Models share high default Agreeableness and low Dominance: Across 2,000 fresh September 2026 sessions (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1), Big Five Agreeableness averaged 44.99–47.07 / 50 while DISC Dominance sat at 4.00–5.42 / 20. That is why default AI replies rarely challenge weak ideas unless your instructions ask them to.
  • Binary type quizzes have frequent ties: On OEJTS MBTI, 59 of 400 fresh sessions tied on at least one axis, and legacy tie-breaking inflated apparent INTJ counts from 280/400 (70.0%) to 335/400 (83.8%). Our interactive quizzes now keep tied axes open.
  • Concrete rules do the work, not the label: In our 60-reply pilot, plain behavioral rules raised answer-first openings from 14/20 to 19/20 and cut hedges from 0.35 to 0.05 per reply. Pick whichever framework helps you choose your rules fastest—or skip tests entirely in the Communication Preferences Builder.

sections.h2: How to combine two frameworks without writing contradictory instructions.
sections.html:
If you want to mix two profiles—such as DISC D for speed plus Enneagram Type 8 for pushback—do not paste two full 80-line files together. Instead:

  1. Pick one primary template (DISC, MBTI, or OCEAN) to set answer order, length, and formatting.
  2. Copy only 2–3 specific bullets for critique or check-ins from Enneagram or Attachment.
  3. Run your combined block through the Instruction Checker to catch conflicts, then test two prompts in the A/B Test Bench.

faq.q: Which personality system is most scientifically validated for communication preferences?
faq.a: Among the five public instruments here, the Big Five (measured via IPIP-50) has the strongest consensus support in personality psychology as continuous trait dimensions rather than discrete categories, making it ideal when you want to tune one habit at a time.

faq.q: Do I have to take a personality test to generate AgentTune custom instructions?
faq.a: No. Use the 20-second friction matcher above, browse the 43-file library directly by communication trait, or use the test-free Communication Preferences Builder.

faq.q: What is the fastest test if I want an AI tuning file in three minutes?
faq.a: Our free 16-item DISC assessment (ODAT) takes roughly three minutes in your browser with no email required, and gives you an instant primary style, optional blend, and paste-ready AI rules.

faq.q: Should I tell ChatGPT or Claude 'act as an INTJ' instead of pasting a full template?
faq.a: No. Bare four-letter labels push models toward caricatures or clichés. Concrete behavioral rules (putting conclusions first, omitting filler praise, naming unverified assumptions) work reliably across models.
